articles.summary: Princeton Bancorp, Inc. (the “Company”) (NASDAQ - BPRN), the bank holding company for The Bank of Princeton (the “Bank”), today reported its unaudited financial condition and results of operations for the quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026. President and CEO Edward Dietzler spoke to the quarter results, "During the third quarter, we charged off two previously identified problem loans and recorded an asset write-down related to a future retail consolidation. While these actions reduced reported net income to $1.0 million for the quarter, excluding these non-recurring items, our Bank's core operations generated approximately $7.0 million plus in net income, demonstrating the underlying strength of our franchise." Quarter over Quarter Highlights Net loans increased by $80.0 million, or 18.1% on an annualized linked-quarter basis Total deposits grew $68.0 million, representing a 14.0% annualized linked-quarter increase Total assets expanded by $57.3 million, or 10.1%
articles.title: Princeton Bancorp Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results

articles.summary: Princeton Bancorp, Inc. (the “Company”) (NASDAQ - BPRN), the bank holding company for The Bank of Princeton (the “Bank”), announced that its Board of Directors, at a meeting held on October 28, 2026, declared a cash dividend of $0.40 per share of the common stock of the Company. This dividend will be paid on November 25, 2026, to shareholders of record at the close of business on November 11, 2026. “This dividend increase is indicative of the Board of Directors and managements' confidence in the performance of the Company and its commitment to providing a strong return to shareholders,” stated Edward Dietzler, President and CEO. The paying of cash dividends on a quarterly basis is subject to a determination and declaration each quarter by its Board of Directors, which will take into account a number of factors, including the financial condition of the Company, and any applicable legal and regulatory restrictions on the payment of dividends by the Company and the Bank.
